title: 〜抜く / 〜ぬく
meaning: do… through to the end / do… despite difficulty (persevere)
simpleExplanation: Verb stem + 抜く means "push through to the end no matter how hard it is": 走り抜く "run all the way", やり抜く "see it through", 耐え抜く "endure to the end". While 切る focuses on finishing, 抜く focuses on the struggle and determination along the way.
whenUsed: Speeches, sports, motivational writing, biographies: 最後までやり抜く. Also 考え抜く "think something through thoroughly". Not used for easy or routine actions.
formation: Verb ます-stem + 抜く (Group 1 verb: 抜いた, 抜いて, 抜きます)
Common: やり抜く, 走り抜く, 生き抜く, 考え抜く, 耐え抜く, 戦い抜く

diagram.title: 抜く vs 切る vs 通す

rows.label: 〜抜く
cells: 苦しくてもやり抜く (see it through even if it's painful)

rows.label: 〜切る
cells: Complete, use up, to the extreme
本を読み切る (finish the whole book)

rows.label: 〜通す
cells: Keep the same thing all the way
一年間、無遅刻を通す (keep a perfect record all year)

examples.reading: さいごまではしりぬいた。
examples.en: I ran through to the very end.
examples.note: Sports: ran to the very end.

examples.ja: 苦しくてもやり抜くつもりだ。
examples.reading: くるしくてもやりぬくつもりだ。
examples.en: Even if it's hard, I intend to see it through.
examples.note: やり抜く = the set phrase for 'see it through'.

examples.ja: よく考え抜いて決めた。
examples.reading: よくかんがえぬいてきめた。
examples.en: I thought it over thoroughly before deciding.
examples.note: 考え抜く = think through thoroughly (persistence of thought).

examples.ja: 祖父は戦争の時代を生き抜いた人だ。
examples.reading: そふはせんそうのじだいをいきぬいたひとだ。
examples.en: My grandfather is someone who survived the war years.
examples.note: 生き抜く = live through hardship.

examples.ja: 厳しい練習に耐え抜いて、彼はプロになった。
examples.reading: きびしいれんしゅうにたえぬいて、かれはプロになった。
examples.en: Having endured the harsh training to the end, he became a professional.
examples.note: 耐え抜く = endure to the end.

similarGrammar.difference: Emphasises completion or using everything up, not effort. 読み切る (finish reading) vs 読み抜く (rare).
'Carry through consistently' (やり通す is close to やり抜く; 隠し通す = keep hidden all the way).
Neutral continuation, no sense of difficulty.

commonMistakes.wrong: 毎朝コーヒーを飲み抜く。
commonMistakes.why: 抜く needs a hard or long task; routine actions do not take it.
抜く attaches to the ます-stem (やり), not the dictionary form.

commonMistakes.wrong: ご飯を食べ抜いた。(meaning 'ate it all')
commonMistakes.why: Finishing food is completion, so 切る is right; 抜く would suggest a heroic struggle.

usageNotes: 抜く also has independent meanings: 'pull out' (歯を抜く), 'skip' (朝食を抜く), 'overtake' (前の車を抜く). Only the compound use is covered here.
The set 最後までやり抜く appears in speeches and slogans.
考え抜いた末に 'after thinking it through' is a common narrative phrase.
jlptTips: Keywords such as 最後まで, 苦しくても, 厳しい, あきらめずに point to 抜く.
If the verb is about eating, reading or using up, the answer is 切る rather than 抜く.
Only a limited set of verbs takes 抜く; when unsure, choose it with やる, 走る, 生きる, 考える, 耐える, 戦う.
